name: North Carolina
headline_status: Recreational and comprehensive medical cannabis are illegal in North Carolina; only a narrow low-THC hemp-extract law for epilepsy exists.
summary: Cannabis remains illegal under North Carolina state law, though possessing a half ounce or less is a Class 3 misdemeanor for which any jail sentence must be suspended. The state's only medical provision is a 2014 law allowing low-THC, high-CBD hemp extract for intractable epilepsy. The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians runs its own legal adult-use market on tribal land. Gov. Josh Stein created an Advisory Council on Cannabis in June 2025, which in April 2026 flagged the unregulated intoxicating hemp market and is due to deliver final recommendations by December 31, 2026.

medical_since.value: 2014, when HB 1220 allowed hemp extract for epilepsy (pilot designation removed in 2015 by HB 766). There is no comprehensive medical program.

medical_program.value: Limited to hemp extract with less than 0.9% THC and at least 5% CBD by weight for intractable epilepsy.

possession_limit.value: No legal possession amount for adults under state law.

penalties.value: Up to 0.5 oz is a Class 3 misdemeanor with any jail sentence suspended; over 0.5 oz is a Class 1 misdemeanor; over 1.5 oz (or over 3/20 oz of hashish) is a Class I felony.

retail_sales.value: No state-licensed sales. The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians has sold adult-use cannabis to adults 21+ on its land since September 7, 2024.

hemp_thc.value: Intoxicating hemp-derived THC products are sold with no clear state rules on potency, testing or labeling; the governor's cannabis council called this a dangerous policy gap in April 2026.

purchase_age.value: No state-legal purchase. The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians has sold adult-use cannabis to adults 21+ on its tribal land since September 2024; state law still bans possession elsewhere.

public_use.value: Not allowed anywhere: there is no legal recreational or medical marijuana use, so using it in public or private can lead to possession charges.

tourists.value: Only on Cherokee tribal land, where the Eastern Band sells to adults 21+. Elsewhere in North Carolina there are no legal sales, out-of-state medical cards are not recognized, and possession is a crime.

home_grow.value: Not allowed; manufacturing, including cultivating, marijuana is a felony under state law.

dui.value: Impairment-based: North Carolina has no THC per se or zero-tolerance law, so a cannabis DUI requires evidence of impairment.

faq.q: Is weed legal in North Carolina?
faq.a: No. Recreational and medical marijuana are illegal under state law; the only exception is low-THC hemp extract for epilepsy. The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians sells legally on its own tribal land.

faq.q: What happens if you get caught with weed in North Carolina?
faq.a: A half ounce or less is a Class 3 misdemeanor and any jail time must be suspended. Larger amounts bring a Class 1 misdemeanor, and more than 1.5 ounces is a felony.

faq.q: Is medical marijuana legal in North Carolina?
faq.a: No comprehensive program exists. Medical bills have passed the Senate in past sessions but not the House.

faq.q: Can you buy weed in Cherokee, North Carolina?
faq.a: Yes. The Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians has sold adult-use cannabis to adults 21+ on its land since September 7, 2024.
